players.name: Mauro Tassotti
players.note: An ever-present and an excellent club right-back, never a fixture for Italy.

players.name: Franco Baresi
players.note: Thirty-one and at the height of it: the libero of the unbeaten side and an all-time great at the position.

players.name: Paolo Maldini
players.note: Twenty-three and already Italy’s left-back, but not yet the player of his mid-nineties peak.

players.name: Marco van Basten
players.note: Ballon d’Or and capocannoniere in the strongest league in the world; a complete centre-forward at his peak.

players.name: Sebastiano Rossi
players.note: First season as the first choice; very good, and never Italy’s keeper.

players.name: Frank Rijkaard
players.note: Peak years. Played across centre-back and midfield, so no single role describes him.

players.name: Alessandro Costacurta
players.note: Twenty-five and an established starter in the best defence in the world; short of his own peak.

players.name: Ruud Gullit
players.note: Back in the side after the knee operations — short of 1987 but still world class.

players.name: Demetrio Albertini
players.note: Nineteen, and twenty-two starts into the side already; the passing was there, the rest came later.

players.name: Carlo Ancelotti
players.note: Thirty-two, knees gone, in his final season — ten starts and a long way below the midfielder he had been.

players.name: Marco Simone
players.note: Seven goals in seven starts at twenty-two, off the bench as often as not.

players.name: Filippo Galli
players.note: A genuinely good centre-half who was fourth choice behind Baresi, Costacurta and Maldini.

players.name: Francesco Antonioli
players.note: Twenty-one and the reserve keeper; a long, solid Serie A career followed.

players.name: Diego Fuser
players.note: Twenty-two and on the fringe; four goals in four hundred minutes, most of them struck from distance.
